description.text: Our mission is to accelerate the mastery of biology to advance human health. We are a life sciences technology company focused on building innovative products and solutions to interrogate, understand and master biology. Our integrated research solutions include instruments, consumables and software for analyzing biological systems at a resolution and scale that matches the complexity of biology. We have built deep expertise across diverse disciplines including chemistry, biology, hardware and software. Innovations in all of these areas have enabled the deployment of our rapidly expanding suite of products, which allow our customers to interrogate biological systems at previously inaccessible resolution and scale. Our products have enabled researchers to make fundamental discoveries across multiple areas of biology, including oncology, immunology and neuroscience. Since launching our first product in mid-2015 through December 31, 2025, we have sold 8,046 instruments to researchers around the world, including academic and translational researchers and biopharmaceutical companies. Our revenue was $642.8 million and $610.8 million for the years ended 2025 and 2024, respectively, representing a year-over-year increase of 5%. We generated net losses of $43.5 million and $182.6 million for the years ended 2025 and 2024, respectively. In the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we sold 1,007 and 1,073 instruments and 424,000 and 357,100 consumable reactions, respectively.

Our integrated research solutions include instruments, consumables and software for single cell and spatial biology, which help academic and translational researchers and biopharmaceutical companies understand biological systems at a resolution and scale that matches the complexity of biology. Our products are behind breakthroughs in oncology, immunology, neuroscience and more, fueling powerful discoveries that are transforming the world's understanding of health and disease.

analysis_md:
# TXG — 10x Genomics, Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-19. Price $71.95 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $8.975B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Life-science tools: instruments, consumables and software for single-cell and spatial biology — Chromium (single cell), Visium and Xenium (spatial), plus the new Atera spatial platform launching through H2 2026. Razor/blade model: Q2 2026 revenue was $151.0M, of which consumables were $130.8M (Single Cell $88.5M, Spatial $42.3M, +16.2% YoY), instruments $7.7M and services $10.7M (Q2 2026 release, via search). Customers are academic, translational and biopharma labs, so demand rides research budgets.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $136,050,000; capex $5,935,000; SBC $109,118,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $20,997,000 = $0.17/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $0.17) — the first positive FY in the last 5 (OE-positive years 1/5).
- Maintenance version FY2025 (financials_history.csv): $52,376,000 — higher than the conservative figure because it adds back D&A above the capex cap; the conservative OCF-based figure is the one used, and the gap is the SBC-heavy cost structure, not a one-off. Note the maintenance construction (net income + D&A − capex − ΔNWC) embeds the FY2025 working-capital release quantified under NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below; it is not a cleaner measure here.
- Capex completeness: the engine's capex leg reads PP&E purchases only. statements.json carries a second capex-type line — purchases of intangibles/software (PaymentsToAcquireIntangibleAssets): $923,000 (FY2023), $1,000,000 (FY2024), $0 (FY2025), and none filed in any quarter of the TTM window. Restating for it: FY2023 OE/share -$1.98 (from -$1.97), FY2024 OE/share -$1.22 and the normalized median stays -$1.22 (unchanged at quote precision); FY2025 OE and the TTM base are untouched because the line is $0 in both. The CSV stands as the engine produced it; the omission is disclosed here rather than patched by hand, and it cannot move any tier.
- The three prior years were deeply negative on the same definition: FY2023 OE/share -$1.97, FY2024 -$1.22 (financials_history.csv), because SBC peaked at $166,950,000 in FY2023 while operating cash flow was still negative.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $136,050,000 − prior YTD $52,059,000 + current YTD $43,094,000 = **TTM $127,085,000**
- Capex: FY $5,935,000 − prior YTD $3,471,000 + current YTD $3,185,000 = **TTM $5,649,000**
- SBC: FY $109,118,000 − prior YTD $58,635,000 + current YTD $48,258,000 = **TTM $98,741,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **129,050,312**
- **TTM OE total $22,695,000 → base OE/share $0.18** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is **-$1.22/share** — it is the FY2024 figure, from the window where SBC was $140.7–167.0M and OCF was ~zero. It is not used as the scoring base because the TTM window is fresher: FY2025 OE turned positive (+$0.17/share) and the TTM through Q2 2026 prints +$0.18/share on falling SBC ($167.0M FY2023 → $141M FY2024 → $109.1M FY2025 → $98.7M TTM). Both positive prints, however, are working-capital-assisted — see the NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE resolution — which is why the final tier is F despite the D by numbers. The method range: Tier F on the median base and Tier F on the TTM base ex-release (≈ -$0.33/share); Tier D only on the TTM base as filed, with an IV@15% of $1.68. Either way it is nowhere near the $71.95 price — the base choice does not change the investment conclusion, only the letter.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, real platform, unproven economics
Justification: integrated Chromium/Visium/Xenium installed base with recurring consumables, workflow switching costs and a court-validated patent estate, capped at 5 because returns on capital are negative in every measured year and gross margin compressed ~16pp from its peak before recovering.
- FOR: largest installed base in single cell and spatial — Chromium, Visium and Xenium as one integrated instrument + consumables + software ecosystem; razor/blade pull-through (Q2 2026 consumables $130.8M of $151.0M revenue, Spatial consumables +16.2% YoY); patent estate that wins in court (2026 Delaware jury: three Scale Biosciences single-cell patents valid and willfully infringed by Qiagen's Parse unit, 14% royalty); high gross-margin structure (69.1% FY2025, 70.0% TTM in fundamentals.json, ~74% in Q2 2026 per the Q2 release); workflow/data switching costs — lab protocols, pipelines and published datasets standardize on 10x formats.
- AGAINST: no returns on capital yet — the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is negative every year 2021–2025 (-17.9%, -22.6%, -54.9%, -42.0%, -14.9%) and operating income is negative in every filed year, so there is no ROIC-above-cost-of-capital evidence for a higher score; gross margin compressed from 84.9% (2021) to 66.2% (2023) before recovering to 69.1% (2025) / 70.0% TTM — pricing power is contested; real competition (Bruker CosMx ex-NanoString, Vizgen MERSCOPE, Akoya in spatial; Parse/Qiagen and Illumina in single cell); SBC consumes the cash ($98.7M TTM vs $127.1M TTM OCF) and the diluted count grows 3.1%/yr with no buyback; growth has stalled to low single digits ex-settlement and demand is academic/government-budget exposed.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — 5.4 final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check (written, per spec): the engine's blended growth is 4.48% (components: rev CAGR 5y 16.56%, rev CAGR 3y 7.57%, latest rev YoY 5.25%, share-count adjustment -3.09pp). Recent prints: FY2025 revenue +5.25%; Q2 2026 revenue +3% YoY excluding non-recurring patent-litigation settlement revenue in both periods (the headline -$12.6% is the settlement comparison, per the Q2 release); FY2026 guidance was raised to a $620M midpoint — below FY2025's settlement-inflated $642.8M on a headline basis, i.e. low-single-digit underlying growth. The base start of 4.5% sits just above the ex-settlement prints because Spatial consumables are growing double-digit and Atera ships in H2 2026; the bear start of -0.5% matches the headline guidance decline; the super-bull start of 16.5% equals the 5-yr revenue CAGR and requires the spatial/Atera ramp to fully land — it is a stretch case, which is why it carries only 10%. Default offsets (-12/-5/0/+5/+12pp), default OE multipliers (0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25) and default probabilities (10/25/30/25/10) were kept: the evidence supports no narrower distribution on a base this small.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above.
- **DILUTION** (share count +3.1%/yr, already deducted via the -3.09pp growth adjustment): the SBC trend is improving but from a very high level — $166,950,000 (FY2023) → $140,749,000 (FY2024) → $109,118,000 (FY2025) → $98,741,000 TTM (ttm.json / financials_history.csv). SBC is still 78% of TTM operating cash flow ($98.7M of $127.1M), and the diluted count rose from 117,165,036 (FY2023) to 124,749,885 (FY2025) to 129,050,312 on the TTM share basis, with no buyback to offset it. Dilution is a real, ongoing per-share drag, not a legacy artifact.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: no divestiture, big M&A or restatement — the >60% jump is the 2020→2021 revenue surge ($298,845,000 → $490,490,000, financials_history.csv) as pandemic-era research demand pulled single-cell adoption forward, on an as-filed basis throughout. The related distortion is license/settlement revenue: Q1 2025 carried $17,060,000 of license and royalty revenue vs $947,000 in Q1 2026, and Q2 2025 carried a large patent-litigation settlement (Q2 2026 release, via search), which is why headline YoY revenue prints swing from -12.6% to +3% ex-settlement. Growth inputs were therefore anchored on the recent ex-settlement prints and guidance, not on the 5-yr CAGR that straddles the surge.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): the bridge is non-cash SBC + D&A, not a one-off tax deposit or impairment. FY2025: net income -$43,544,000 vs OCF +$136,050,000, with SBC $109,118,000 and D&A $36,199,000 added back (financials_history.csv). FY2023: net income -$255,099,000 vs OCF -$15,197,000, SBC $166,950,000 + D&A $35,512,000. FY2024: net income -$182,627,000 vs OCF +$6,664,000, SBC $140,749,000 + D&A $35,879,000. Because the base is OCF-based and SBC is deducted in full, the divergence does not flatter the base — it is the reason the base is only $0.18/share. The bridge also contains a large working-capital release that the SBC + D&A lines alone do not explain: FY2025 delta_nwc is -$65,656,000 (financials_history.csv), a net release of $65,656,000 into OCF — the big cash-flow lines are receivables -$41,314,000 and inventories -$27,953,000 (balances falling, cash in; statements.json), partly offset by smaller lines. Excluding that release, FY2025 OCF is ≈ $70,394,000 and FY2025 conservative OE is ≈ -$44,659,000 (-$0.36/share): the FY2025 positive print is WC-assisted. The TTM window is worse, not better: bridging TTM OCF from the cash-flow lines (statements.json quarterly) — net income -$75,125,000 + SBC $98,741,000 + D&A $39,983,000 + other non-cash -$1,443,000 = $62,156,000 against OCF of $127,085,000 — leaves +$64,929,000 of TTM OCF from working-capital / other operating movements. The dominant piece is the collection of the Q2 2025 patent-litigation settlement receivable: other current assets were $69,090,000 at Q2 2025 and $3,084,000 at Q2 2026 (the engine-construction ΔNWC over the window is -$92,078,000; the itemized CF working-capital lines add +$23,588,000, inventory-led). Ex-release TTM OE is therefore ≈ -$42,234,000, about -$0.33/share. Consequence: the positive $0.18 base is entirely release-assisted, and on every adjusted basis (median -$1.22/share; TTM ex-release ≈ -$0.33/share) normalized owner's earnings are negative — the final tier is F via tier_override (tier by numbers stays D on the as-filed TTM base). The investment conclusion never depended on the letter: every variant sits ~97% below the $71.95 price.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (2018): that pre-IPO history year uses the outstanding count (14,549,801, FALLBACK:CommonStockSharesOutstanding in financials_history.csv); per-share history there is approximate. 2018 is outside the base window and the growth blend's per-share inputs, so it does not touch the verdict.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK**: stated from the filing — the company carries no funded debt. The FY2025 balance sheet (10-K, via financials_history.csv / fundamentals.json) shows total liabilities of $245,039,000 and equity of $796,326,000 with no borrowings line; the only debt-like item is operating lease liabilities of $84,361,000 (dcf_numbers.json). The Q2 2026 balance sheet (Q2 release, via search) likewise shows cash and equivalents of $502,512,000 and marketable securities of $49,521,000 against operating liabilities only. Net debt is therefore not "unknown leverage" — it is a net-cash balance sheet whose exact net figure the engine leaves blank because no debt tag exists to subtract.
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED**: the FY2025 cash figure of $473,966,000 is filed on the combined cash + restricted-cash tag and no restricted-cash tag separates it in the feed, so the engine's (blank) net-debt figure would overstate net cash by the restricted amount if it computed one (equivalently, net debt would be understated — the direction the flag names). Direction is immaterial here: with no funded debt (above), the company is net cash on any split of that combined figure.
- **IRR_AT_FLOOR**: the weighted IRR of 2.81% sits within 0.5pp of the 2.5% terminal growth rate (super bear, bear, base, bull and weighted all at the floor) — at $71.95 against a $0.18 base, the price is beyond the model's range and the expected return reads "at most ~3%", not the recorded 2.81%. The tier is D on any reading.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (0.24%): correct and central — at this price the valuation rests almost entirely on future growth and SBC normalization, not on current owner's earnings. That is exactly what the verdict sizes to.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.51x): real — super-bull IV@15% is $3.20 against super-bear $0.71. Confidence is capped at low, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end; note even the super-bull IV is 96% below the price, so the spread does not rescue the stock.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range: Tier F on the normalized 3-yr median base (-$1.22/share) and Tier F on the TTM base ex-release (≈ -$0.33/share); only the as-filed TTM base (+$0.18/share, IV@15% $1.68) prints a D, and it is entirely a settlement-receivable collection. All variants agree on the only decision-relevant fact — at $71.95 the market is pricing in an OE trajectory (sustained double-digit growth with SBC falling toward zero as a share of OCF) that no filing period has yet printed.
- The cost inflection is real (SBC has fallen 41% from its FY2023 peak and OCF has improved for three straight periods), but the earnings inflection is a settlement collection, not run-rate OE — and even the as-filed TTM owner's earnings of $22,695,000 support a market cap of $8.975B only at ~395x TTM OE (a ratio of the two quoted figures, stated for scale). Q2 2026 also showed the fragility: instruments fell 47.2% YoY as Xenium customers paused ahead of Atera, and FY2026 guidance of $620M at the midpoint is a headline decline.
- Balance sheet is not the risk: no funded debt, $473,966,000 of combined cash at FY2025 ($502,512,000 cash + $49,521,000 marketable securities at Q2 2026 per the Q2 release), lease liabilities $84,361,000. The risk is purely the price versus the OE base, plus academic-budget exposure and spatial competition (Bruker, Vizgen, Akoya, Illumina's entry, Parse/Qiagen).
- What would change the verdict: scale, not direction. The model is linear in the base: IV@15% of $1.68 on the $0.18 as-filed base reaches the $71.95 price only at ≈ 43x the base (≈ $7.55/share, ≈ $974M of OE — OCF of ≈ $1.08B at the current SBC/capex run-rate). SBC falling below ~$50M/yr while OCF holds above ~$150M would roughly quadruple the as-filed base (≈ $0.73/share, IV@15% ≈ $7) — a genuine inflection, but still Tier D, not a verdict change. Only Atera driving a return to double-digit revenue growth with OE leverage compounds toward the 43x; neither is in the filings yet.

## Final verdict
